I could rate this GP practice below zero, I absolutely would. I am livid. Dr John should not be allowed anywhere near children, let alone be practising medicine.

Two weeks ago, my son had a high fever. I managed to bring it down and called for an appointment. Dr John rang back saying, “Come in, I’ll check him,” claiming he could hear wheezing over the phone. Brilliant start, right? When we got there, he barely looked at my child and said, “No temperature, nothing wrong, just keep giving paracetamol.” Because apparently, according to him, everything can be fixed with paracetamol and a shrug.

My son kept getting worse — he couldn’t breathe properly — so we called again. And yet again Dr John dismissed us with, “I saw him last week, he was fine.” He rushed us in, did a one-minute “examination” (if you can even call it that), and then repeated his favourite line: “There’s nothing wrong.” I asked him to check the throat, tonsils, anything — he barely bothered to look. “All good, keep giving paracetamol.” And sent us home. The level of neglect is genuinely shocking.

Thankfully, I trusted my instincts and took my child to a private clinic. And surprise, surprise: EVERYTHING Dr John said was wrong. Completely wrong. My son had pus-covered tonsils, an enlarged adenoid the size of a walnut, and a blocked ear — he was practically deaf on one side. His oxygen level was 93. For a nearly 3-year-old, it should be above 95. The private doctor said it was only a matter of time before things got seriously dangerous — the infection could have spread to the ears or even the brain.

I want an explanation — a real one — as to why a doctor would treat patients with such complete lack of attention and care. It is an absolute shame to the profession. Someone who dismisses a struggling, sick child so casually should not be practising medicine at all. This behaviour is not just unprofessional; it is unsafe and unacceptable.

My son is now on THREE antibiotics and additional medication, yet according to Dr John, there was “nothing wrong” and “no need for treatment.” Disgraceful. It's good that there are other clinics we can turn to, I don't know what would have happened to my child if I had done what the doctor in question told me once again.
